Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

Class features.
Spell automation.

Character abilities, weapon masteries, feat benefits, and spell-specific helpers connected to your native rolls and chat cards.

Automations → Unique Classes

Class features

Damage choices appear in the native roll’s Configuration area, with a live dice preview. Once-per-turn choices show No - Already Used when unavailable. The module’s class filter includes all twelve core classes; the sections below cover classes with specific automations.

Barbarian

  • Reckless Attack The first attack roll of your turn offers Reckless. It applies the feature effect and recommends advantage on qualifying Strength attacks until your next turn starts, including reaction attacks. Attacks against the Reckless creature also receive advantage, with normal disadvantage cancellation.
  • Frenzy While Rage and Reckless Attack are active, the first qualifying Strength-based weapon hit on your turn includes the feature’s bonus damage automatically. It matches the weapon damage type, supports criticals, and shows No - Already Used after use.

Monk

  • Stunning Strike On a qualifying Monk-weapon or Unarmed Strike hit, damage Configuration offers a default-No choice. Confirming Yes spends 1 Focus Point and prompts the native Constitution save, once per combat turn.
  • Failed and successful saves Failure applies Stunned. Success halves Speed and grants advantage on the next attack against the creature. These effects last until the start of the Monk’s next turn.
  • Stun before Grapple When combined with Grapple, Stunning Strike resolves first, including its animation and automatic effects. A Stunned target automatically fails the following Strength/Dexterity save.
  • Independent corrections Undo Effect restores the Apply control and unlocks Stunning Strike’s rolled save adjustments independently of weapon damage. Reapplication locks its save again.

Shared Grapple / Prone prompts are under Common; Grappler’s feat benefits have their own Feats setting.

Paladin

  • Divine Smite Eligible melee weapon hit damage offers the feature’s available free cast or a spell-slot selection. The chosen resource and bonus action are consumed; slot-funded casts also use the character spell-slot tracker.
  • Fiend and Undead bonus A golden glow and underline indicate that the target qualifies for an extra d8. The info icon explains the bonus. Damage scales with the selected slot and follows the attack’s critical damage.

Ranger

  • Hunter’s Prey / Colossus Slayer Adds the configured extra damage against an injured single target, once per combat turn. The selector initially defaults to No and remembers the previous choice. Full-health targets disable it; damage matches the weapon and supports criticals.

Hunter’s Mark is grouped with Spells because its rider follows the caster’s concentration and marked target.

Rogue

  • Sneak Attack Damage Configuration defaults to Yes after an attack with advantage and No otherwise. The player or GM can select it when another qualifying circumstance applies; this is assistance, not a complete eligibility ruling.
  • Damage and timing Uses the feature’s configured damage and the weapon’s damage type, including critical support. The once-per-turn marker resets at the end of the current combat turn, allowing a later qualifying reaction attack. Canceling does not consume it.

Sorcerer

  • Innate Sorcery While its effect is active, Sorcerer spell attacks recommend advantage. Other classes’ spells and weapon attacks are excluded; other advantage/disadvantage sources still combine normally.
  • Transmuted Spell Choose an eligible elemental damage type before rolling. The choice follows subsequent damage from that casting, with no repeated Sorcery Point charge.
  • Heightened Spell Choose one target before its save. Disadvantage combines with other sources, so Magic Resistance can cancel it to a normal save.
  • Careful Spell Select protected creatures before rolling. It records automatic successes and prevents half-on-save damage for those creatures. Protection does not remove targets from a nonselective spell.
  • Empowered Spell The spell damage card offers a feature-icon action. Select active damage dice up to the Charisma modifier, minimum one, then confirm to spend 1 Sorcery Point and keep the new results, even when lower. Opening the picker hands automatic application back to manual control; applied damage must first be undone.
  • Seeking Spell A missed spell attack offers a reroll action. Spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll one d20 and use the new result; linked hit/critical results update, with a damage prompt on a hit.
  • Costs, combinations, and card tags Cast-time choices respect supported Sorcery Incarnate / active Innate Sorcery combination limits and Arcane Apotheosis free-use accounting. Empowered and Seeking remain result-card options. Tags show the applied Metamagic, with element and target details in tooltips.

Warlock

  • Eldritch Smite An eligible pact-weapon hit offers a default-No damage rider. Yes spends a Pact Magic slot, scales Force damage with that slot’s level, and marks the feature used for the combat turn. It does not consume a bonus action.

Hex, Conjure Minor Elementals, and the Eldritch Blast remaining-attacks window are described under Spells.

Automations → Weapon Masteries

Weapon masteries

The actor must have the mastery unlocked in its native D&D5e configuration. The main Effect Automation switch controls the group; turning it off greys out the individual options while preserving their selections.

  • Sap Applies on a hit and recommends disadvantage on the victim’s next attack.
  • Vex Applies after damage and recommends advantage on the attacker’s next attack against that target.
  • Slow Applies a non-stacking 10-foot speed reduction after damage, lasting until the source’s next turn starts.
  • Topple A hit-only card action prompts a Constitution save through the defender’s owner or GM, with a source-tracked Prone effect on failure.
  • Graze A miss automatically creates its flat damage card using the attack ability modifier and weapon damage type. It follows damage automation and supports Undo Damage. Undo hides that card and restores the linked attack’s Damage/Graze controls.

Push, Nick, and Cleave remain manual.

Automations → Feats

Feat benefits

  • Savage Attacker Defaults to Yes when available. Rolls weapon damage dice as two complete sets and keeps the higher total, with both sets available in the result details. A used marker enforces its limit until next turn start; canceling does not consume it. Normal/Critical corrections after Undo retain cached results.
  • Grappler Preserves damage plus Grapple once on your turn and recommends advantage against creatures grappled by that attacker. Later attempts replace damage, and Prone never keeps the damage. This feat toggle is separate from the Common unarmed-prompt setting.

Unarmed Grapple / Prone prompts

Available to any creature using a qualifying action-based Unarmed, Empowered, or Elemental Strike hit; bonus-action and reaction attacks are excluded. Choose No, Grapple, or Prone in damage Configuration. Attempts replace damage unless the separate Grappler benefit is enabled and available.

The target uses its higher Strength/Dexterity save modifier, choosing Strength on ties. The DC uses the attacker’s Strength, or Dexterity when Martial Arts allows it. Separate save cards leave existing item Grapple/Shove activities untouched. Grappled is a Temporary effect for token HUD visibility without a timed expiry.

Stunning Strike resolves before a linked Grapple save. When Stunned applies, the following save is recorded as an automatic failure; otherwise the normal save is prompted. Effects follow the table’s application settings and support Undo.

Automations → Spells

Spell-specific helpers

  • Shield assistance Provides Shield-related chat-card assistance. Retarget can refresh hit/miss results after an AC change while retaining the original attack dice; applied damage requires its own Undo.
  • Hex and Hunter’s Mark Follow the caster’s concentration and single marked target. Yes in damage Configuration adds the labeled Necrotic/Force rider to the existing damage card. Changing the mark’s recorded target updates its association. Hunter’s Mark can apply its configured utility effect through GM automation; Hex retains its effect-selection step.
  • Conjure Minor Elementals Checks whether the single attack target is inside that caster’s concentrated spell Region. Its configured Bonus Attack Damage activity and cast level supply the damage. The elemental selector in the damage row remembers the last Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning choice.
  • Configured buff effects Optional utility-effect application uses the effects already configured on the activity, with native duration and concentration handling.

Eldritch Blast and Scorching Ray

A Pending Attacks window counts remaining shots by character level or cast level. Each attack uses the current single target and native attack/damage cards without another slot spend. Canceling a roll does not consume a shot; the window closes when none remain.
